rows.text: Mortimer breathed out through his nose, a small administrative rejection of the afternoon. The smell of smoked meat lingered with the confidence of something that had never needed approval.
The awning gave a small creak, as though submitting a complaint it knew would be ignored. The smell of salt and fat continued without waiting for approval.
The machine gave a small, apologetic hiss. Gerald narrowed his eyes at it; apparently even the equipment was struggling to meet the minimum standard of being worth his time.
Gerald gives you a small nod as the machine lets out a weary hiss. Approval has clearly been granted, though the equipment has filed a separate objection.

Flick shifted with a faint scrape, maintaining the careful distance of someone who suspected friendliness came with a subscription fee. A little dust settled between you, apparently satisfied with the arrangement.
A dry click rises from the basin, followed by a faint smell of warm stone. Even the silence here appears to be waiting for someone else to take responsibility.
Portia emitted a tiny grinding noise, the architectural equivalent of leaving someone on read. A little dust settled with the air of paperwork that had successfully become somebody else's problem.
The archway gave a small, companionable creak as you passed beneath it. Structural approval was much like ordinary approval, except that withdrawal involved considerably more rubble.
A page rustled with the weary precision of a complaint being filed. Marginalia remained unimpressed, a position requiring no evidence and therefore admirably easy to maintain.
A page rustled behind you, then stopped, apparently unwilling to provide further evidence. The smell of old paper lingered with the quiet confidence of something exempt from rent.
The air gave a tiny, papery crackle. Even silence here seemed to be awaiting approval, which explained why it had accomplished so little.
A faint crackle followed your footsteps, half a beat late. Even the end of the world apparently had buffering.
